example.question: In Prudential International Assurance plc's Solvency and Financial Condition Report for the year ended 31 December 2025, Solvency II technical provisions (gross of reinsurance) are lower than those in the FRS 102/103 financial statements. What is the total difference at 31 December 2025 in £ million, which line of business accounts for the largest part of it, and what share of the total difference does that line represent (one decimal)?
example.question_natural: By how much were PIA's end-2025 Solvency II technical provisions below its financial statements, and which business line drove most of the gap (amount and share)?
example.reference_answer: At 31 December 2025 Solvency II technical provisions were £546m lower than in the financial statements (£10,220m vs £10,766m). The largest contributor was Insurance with profit participation, with a difference of £416m (financial statements £8,419m vs Solvency II £8,004m), i.e. 416 / 546 = about 76.2% of the total difference. The other components were Unit Linked Insurance £98m, Other life insurance £102m, and the Risk Margin (69), which exists only under Solvency II and therefore reduces the difference.

evidence.text: The differences in methods and assumptions result in the Solvency II technical provisions (gross of reinsurance) being lower by £546m than those shown in the financial statements.

example.question: In Belfius' 2025 annual results press release (consolidated, unaudited key figures of the management report), rank the four outstanding loan segments (Mortgage & Consumer Loans, Business, Corporate, Public & Social) by percentage growth in outstanding loans between 31 December 2024 (as adjusted for the new segmentation) and 31 December 2025, computing growth from the published figures in EUR billion (one decimal). example.reference_answer: Based on the published figures: 1) Mortgage & Consumer Loans: €49.6 billion to €52.7 billion, +6.25% (about +6.3%); 2) Corporate: €26.3 billion to €27.5 billion, about +4.6%; 3) Business: €18.2 billion to €18.9 billion, about +3.8%; 4) Public & Social: €24.2 billion to €24.3 billion, about +0.4% (the release's text gives +0.5%).
